scope: Proposition 7.4 (Weighted shell conversion) of the manuscript “The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions” (preprints/The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 073 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 98a7e721547308b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 ≤ a ≤ v ≤ N be integer depths, and let X, Y be separated cells at depth a of one or two classes. Let mx(w) and ny(w) be products of the undifferentiated masks at one index i < J0 for two specified indexed descriptor lists. Assume both lists have at most NCA occurrences, where one exponent CA is fixed independently of N for the whole family under consideration, as in Definition 7.1. Let L be the largest nominal length in either list, with L = 0 when both lists are empty. For measurable |f|, |g| ≤ 1 define a possibly complex measure ν on the distance line by ∫︂ F(s) dν(s) = 1 M1(a)M2(a) ∫︂ X×Y F(D(x, y)) (D(x, y)2a )−n∗/2 · f(x)g(y) mx(e(x, y))ny(e(x, y)) dρ1(x)dρ2(y). (7.9) If v − a ≥ 20σN, L ≤ (v − a)/2 + σN, (7.10) then for every fixed T > 0, 2−a ∫︂ 2v+1 2v−1 |ˆ︁ ν(r)|2 dr ≤ Ro(1) sup HF (a, v) + O(R−T ). (7.11) The supremum has the same cells, class normalizations, lists and smoothing index as in Equa- tion (7.9). Its symbols are admissible with a derivative budget and common bounds for smooth angular factors depending only on T, d, CA and the fixed parameters. All these bounds are indepen- dent of N. When f = g = 1, the measure ν is positive. The assertion also holds on the fixed outer supports with a = 0.
